change.m5_rounding_oracle: lua/sector-height-witness.lua forms the expected clearance word in the accepted SSE round-toward-zero profile (toward_zero_single, subtract_single with a two-sum exactness test; division-free); a clean non-dominance (hand-off above the expected value and equal to the control's) is UNREACHED, an incorrectly formed hand-off FAILURE; the scripted harness runs its hand-off under the REAL eech_world::reference_arithmetic::select_sse_toward_zero with MXCSR saved and restored; no C policy, solver, tolerance or baseline change
change.m6_pack_retry: the driver reconciles store_session's pack_session retries (every attempt re-reads every sector): repeats start a new attempt, every attempt must repeat the first in order with the same words, at most 64; the unique final saved-sector relation is what save and load report; inconsistent, omitted or unsupported repetition is NONPASS
change.m6_path_bound: csrc/eech_hw_witness.c: ONE shared helper eech_hw_save_paths bounds BOTH complete writer paths (data and script, suffix and NUL) to the original writer's data_filename [256] and script_filename [256] before any file access and before store_session; called directly by real-C tests (255 accepted, 256 refused for the data and the longer-suffix script path, no output and no file on refusal) and pinned by the source guard against the original writer's buffers
change.consumer_join: same-caller lookahead/move identity with a real answer before eligibility, intervention or consumption; trajectory binding of an intervention window to the paired control report (control=), whole-report validation of original=, control= and expect= (schema 2), strict raw comma-list grammar, request/reply/abort fault precedence over clean UNREACHED, no post-fatal inspection; no created task leader was needed

x11-world-driver-tests.why: the first run of the world targets after the driver rewrite: the host_callbacks census of profile-selecting host scripts failed because the driver's header comment named the profile selection a second time (it pins exactly one occurrence per script); the comment was reworded and x12 passes (a prose-only change of the driver)
